decision.question: How should Notice, NoticeList and NoticeTray be built as Views?
decision.ask: How should Notice, NoticeList and NoticeTray be built as Views?

options.text: All three are Views; the tray owns the list. `class Notice extends View { render(){ p(this.text); button.c('x','×').click(()=>this.dismiss()); } dismiss(){ this.list.remove(this); } }` · `class NoticeList extends View { add(text){ this.append(() => new Notice({text, list:this})); this.tray.count(this.children.length); return this; } remove(n){ n.el.remove(); ...; return this; } clear() }` · `class NoticeTray extends View { render(){ this.bell = button.c('bell').click(()=>this.toggle()); this.list = new NoticeList({tray:this}); } toggle(){} count(n){ this.bell.attr('data-count', n); return this; } }`. Calls go down (tray → list → notice) and come back up by direct method calls on a parent reference.
options.say: All three are Views; the tray owns the list. `class Notice extends View { render(){ p(this.text); button.c('x','×').click(()=>this.dismiss()); } dismiss(){ this.list.remove(this); } }` · `class NoticeList extends View { add(text){ this.append(() => new Notice({text, list:this})); this.tray.count(this.children.length); return this; } remove(n){ n.el.remove(); ...; return this; } clear() }` · `class NoticeTray extends View { render(){ this.bell = button.c('bell').click(()=>this.toggle()); this.list = new NoticeList({tray:this}); } toggle(){} count(n){ this.bell.attr('data-count', n); return this; } }`. Calls go down (tray → list → notice) and come back up by direct method calls on a parent reference.
caveats: Each class holds a reference to its parent, so a Notice cannot be reused outside a NoticeList without passing a fake list.
Badge count is pushed by hand on every add/remove; forget one call and it is wrong.
options.caveat: Each class holds a reference to its parent, so a Notice cannot be reused outside a NoticeList without passing a fake list. Badge count is pushed by hand on every add/remove; forget one call and it is wrong.

options.text: Notice is plain data; NoticeList is the only View with items; NoticeTray wraps it. `class Notice { constructor({text, at}) {...} }` (no DOM) · `class NoticeList extends View { add(notice){ this.items.push(notice); this.draw(notice); this.emit('change'); return this; } draw(n){ div.c('notice', () => { p(n.text); button('×').click(()=>this.remove(n)); }); } }` · `class NoticeTray extends View { render(){ this.bell = button.c('bell').click(()=>this.toggle()); this.list = new NoticeList(); this.list.on('change', () => this.bell.attr('data-count', this.list.items.length)); } }`. Talk is one event, 'change', from list to tray.
options.say: Notice is plain data; NoticeList is the only View with items; NoticeTray wraps it. `class Notice { constructor({text, at}) {...} }` (no DOM) · `class NoticeList extends View { add(notice){ this.items.push(notice); this.draw(notice); this.emit('change'); return this; } draw(n){ div.c('notice', () => { p(n.text); button('×').click(()=>this.remove(n)); }); } }` · `class NoticeTray extends View { render(){ this.bell = button.c('bell').click(()=>this.toggle()); this.list = new NoticeList(); this.list.on('change', () => this.bell.attr('data-count', this.list.items.length)); } }`. Talk is one event, 'change', from list to tray.
caveats: Notice is not a View, so it has no chainable methods of its own and cannot be extended to render differently without overriding NoticeList.draw.
Needs a small event emitter on View (or a DOM CustomEvent); and View.on() handlers cannot be removed.
options.caveat: Notice is not a View, so it has no chainable methods of its own and cannot be extended to render differently without overriding NoticeList.draw. Needs a small event emitter on View (or a DOM CustomEvent); and View.on() handlers cannot be removed.

options.text: All three are Views, and children tell parents through DOM events. `class Notice extends View { render(){ p(this.text); button('×').click(()=>this.dismiss()); } dismiss(){ this.el.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('notice:dismiss', {bubbles:true})); this.el.remove(); return this; } }` · `class NoticeList extends View { add(text){ this.append(()=>new Notice({text})); this.changed(); return this; } count(){ return this.el.children.length; } changed(){ this.el.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('notice:change',{bubbles:true})); } initialize(){ this.el.addEventListener('notice:dismiss', ()=>queueMicrotask(()=>this.changed())); } }` · `class NoticeTray extends View { render(){ this.bell = button.c('bell').click(()=>this.toggle()); this.panel = div.c('dropdown', () => { this.list = new NoticeList(); }); this.el.addEventListener('notice:change', ()=>this.badge()); } toggle(){ this.panel.toggle_class('open'); return this; } badge(){ this.bell.attr('data-count', this.list.count()); return this; } add(text){ this.list.add(text); return this; } }`. Commands go down by method call; news goes up by a bubbling DOM event; the DOM is the only state.
options.say: All three are Views, and children tell parents through DOM events. `class Notice extends View { render(){ p(this.text); button('×').click(()=>this.dismiss()); } dismiss(){ this.el.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('notice:dismiss', {bubbles:true})); this.el.remove(); return this; } }` · `class NoticeList extends View { add(text){ this.append(()=>new Notice({text})); this.changed(); return this; } count(){ return this.el.children.length; } changed(){ this.el.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('notice:change',{bubbles:true})); } initialize(){ this.el.addEventListener('notice:dismiss', ()=>queueMicrotask(()=>this.changed())); } }` · `class NoticeTray extends View { render(){ this.bell = button.c('bell').click(()=>this.toggle()); this.panel = div.c('dropdown', () => { this.list = new NoticeList(); }); this.el.addEventListener('notice:change', ()=>this.badge()); } toggle(){ this.panel.toggle_class('open'); return this; } badge(){ this.bell.attr('data-count', this.list.count()); return this; } add(text){ this.list.add(text); return this; } }`. Commands go down by method call; news goes up by a bubbling DOM event; the DOM is the only state.
caveats: Events are looser than method calls: a typo in an event name fails silently.
Count is read from the DOM, so a hidden or animating-out notice still counts unless removed promptly.
options.caveat: Events are looser than method calls: a typo in an event name fails silently. Count is read from the DOM, so a hidden or animating-out notice still counts unless removed promptly.

decision.why: Option C keeps every piece a real chainable View (house style), lets a Notice live anywhere without a parent reference, and keeps the DOM as the only state, with no new emitter and no on() handlers that cannot be removed. A mistyped event name is the price; listing the names once on NoticeList contains it.
